rationale.conceptual: The method relies on an established but detailed multi-part algorithm: analytical matrix elements for central, bond-bending, and long-range Coulomb forces; secular equation solving; density‑of‑states integration; and Debye temperature root‑finding. It requires careful translation of physics into code, but no novel algorithm or deep research expertise.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 4–6 distinct stages (parameter setup, matrix construction for multiple q‑points, eigenvalue solution, DOS construction, heat capacity calculation, Debye temperature extraction). It involves multiple dependencies (numpy/scipy), but no external data acquisition or complex orchestration. Straightforward I/O in CSV format.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves implementing a 7-parameter bond-bending force model for lattice dynamics of alkali halides. The method uses established harmonic oscillator theory, requiring correct assembly of the dynamical matrix for NaCl structure, including central, bond-bending, and Coulomb (Ewald) contributions. Solving the secular equation and integrating the density of states is conceptually non-trivial but well-documented. Execution involves several stages: matrix construction, diagonalization for high-symmetry points, q-point mesh sampling, DOS integration, and Debye temperature inversion. No large data or GPU needed.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All computations use only 6×6 matrix diagonalizations and moderate q‑point mesh sampling (e.g., 8³ points). No external datasets; model parameters are inline. Memory requirements are minimal (<<1 GB RAM).
